Zambrow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zambrów, Poland

Not demolished. Zambrów's Jewish community, first confirmed at the start of the 18th century, reached 3,216 people (52 percent of the town) by 1921, most killed by the Nazis at Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1943. This cemetery, founded in 1828, was likely used for executions from late June 1941, including of people previously noted to have maintained contact with the USSR. During WWII, Jewish workers were forced by German order to tear down tombstones, later used to pave roads. A 2012 memorial rock now commemorates the cemetery and the local Jewish community.
